item.title: GTA 6 Makes Texting and Driving So Brutal It Might Actually Save Lives IRL
item.description:
GTA 6’s texting-while-driving mechanic is so difficult that it might discourage players from picking up their phones behind the wheel. Here is how the new feature doubles as a real-world road safety lesson, and what fans are saying about it.

GTA 6 Texting While Driving Mechanics Are a Nightmare


Could Teach Millions of Players Not to Text and Drive


Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) features a somewhat realistic portrayal of texting while driving, which could actually benefit viewers in real life. For a franchise known for cultural satire and tackling controversial themes of violence and crime, the popular open-world action-adventure title may teach people a thing or two about keeping their eyes on the road.
According to a November 19, 2026 post on X (Twitter) by Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier, GTA 6 makes driving controls significantly harder when players use their in-game phones, which could discourage people from doing so in real life. “Grand Theft Auto VI could legitimately teach an entire generation not to text while driving, saving millions of lives,” he stated.
Schreier’s post includes a reposted clip showing a player driving one-handed along a beach while looking at their phone and brutally mowing down beachgoers in the process.
Some fans compared the mechanic to the drunk-driving feature in previous GTA titles, where driving under the influence blurs the player's vision and makes steering more difficult. Others jokingly noted that developer Rockstar Games has now done more for road safety than actual driver’s education programs.
There is a certain irony in GTA 6 potentially saving lives by discouraging distracted driving, all while letting players commit virtual murder and mayhem on the very same screen. To know more about our thoughts on Grand Theft Auto 6, check out our review below.

item.title: GTA 6 Cuts Sex Partners, Prostitutes, and Other Longtime Features, Rockstar Explains Why
item.description:
GTA 6 leaves out a classic open-world feature to solicit adult services, a feature dating back to GTA 3. Find out Rockstar's explanation for their choice and the initial fan reaction.
GTA 6 Walkthrough and Guides Wiki

GTA 6 Leaves Some Longtime Series Traditions Behind


GTA 6 Drops the Ability to Solicit Adult Services


In Grand Theft Auto 6, players can no longer solicit prostitutes, ending a series tradition that’s been around since GTA 3. As fans and early reviews have documented, this feature isn’t in the launch version, and there’s currently no similar mechanic in the game.
In a Q&A with Rockstar, we asked if Jason and Lucia can have intimate relationships or sleep with others outside their partnership. Rockstar Vice President of Design Stephen Donkin didn’t give a direct answer. Instead, he talked about the overall design philosophy for GTA 6 and why some familiar features were left out.
"GTA 6 is a game about a couple in a bind, lovers on the run," Donkin said. "While we have taken a lot forward from previous GTA titles, everything we have implemented in 6 has been done to support the spirit of the story we wanted to tell, and the gameplay systems we wanted to expand upon." He pointed out that Rockstar focused on improving the radio, wanted system, robberies, and car theft.
Donkin also said that "many aspects of previous titles are not present in GTA 6," since the studio focused on features that fit Jason and Lucia’s story. He didn’t list which features were removed, but in a separate interview with Kotaku, he confirmed that players can’t gamble at Leonida’s casinos, explaining that gambling didn’t fit the story and could upset the in-game economy.

Some GTA 6 Fans Want the Freedom to Make Jason Cheat on Lucia


Many longtime fans are unhappy with the change and have shared their frustrations on social media. Some question why Jason and Lucia’s relationship should limit these activities, since past GTA protagonists had more freedom to act outside the main story. In the previous title, players noted that GTA 5 let Michael solicit prostitutes even though he was married to Amanda.
Some fans have been more direct, saying they want the option to have Jason cheat on Lucia. Players have discussed whether infidelity could affect the couple’s relationship or change the story’s outcome. Others hoped the game would allow them to pursue other romantic interests like Mandy, a popular early-game side character who flirts with Jason and is suggested to be violent and possibly a serial killer.

Jason and Lucia’s Romance Is Supposed to Be Optional


Player Choice Only Goes So Far in GTA 6


Jason and Lucia will spend much of GTA 6 working together regardless of how close they become. In a September interview with Famitsu, Rockstar North Head of Development and Co-Studio Head Rob Nelson made clear that the romance itself is optional, saying, "whether they go through those situations together as a couple or simply as accomplices is up to the player."
The effort players put into the relationship affects what Jason and Lucia can do together, as Nelson told Famitsu that if players ignore the romance, they lose affectionate actions like holding hands and kissing, but investing in the relationship brings them back.
Players who aren’t interested in romance can still finish the story with Jason and Lucia as partners in crime. Still, fans have pointed out that these statements contrast with the removal of these nightlife activities, as it takes away one of the ways players could previously make choices outside a protagonist’s established relationship.
GTA 6 still offers players a lot of freedom, but Rockstar is setting clearer limits on the story. In keeping Jason and Lucia’s relationship the core of the story, the game had to sacrifice some of its older open-world freedoms that, historically, didn’t affect the main narrative. item.title: Wuthering Waves 4.0 Reveals Exclusive Details with Cryptic Clues for 7 New Characters
item.description:
Wuthering Waves gears up for Version 4.0 with a new 2D animated trailer and seven new characters coming, starting December 22nd.

Wuthering Waves Version 4.0 To Welcome Seven New Characters


Seven Characters, with Lucia Expy Gordia


Wuthering Waves's newest 2D animated trailer, “Beneath Promeus’s Embrace,” revealed the seven new characters slated for release in the upcoming major chapter. While the character Anna was already revealed earlier on in Version 3.8, she will now debut as a playable Resonator sometime in the future. The following characters will also make their appearances in the game throughout 4.X, each with their own unique cryptic phrase that appears to hint at their future roles in the narrative:
 Anna - Roses and Desires
 April - Truth and Illusion
 Cairn - Blood Debts and Purifying Rain
 Gordia - Silent and Honed
 IYA - UFOs and Sparkles
 Lucielle - Future & Falsehoods
 Simulsys - Bones and Bygones

The official visuals for the new Resonators are now available on Wuthering Waves’ official social media channels. One character in particular has caught the eye of some eagle-eyed fans: Gordia’s design suggests that she is an expy (a character from a developer or franchise’s previous title appearing in another, like an Easter Egg) of Punishing Gray Raven’s (PGR) Lucia. Cairn also is visually similar to PGR’s Watanabe.

“Beneath Promeus’s Embrace” Trailer Reveals More of the New Federation


Wuthering Waves also revealed the upcoming location and the title of the newest major chapter. Through the animated trailer, players get to see the new stop in Rover’s journey for the first time: New Federation, a Western-inspired location. Each of the seven new Resonators appear in the trailer, presenting different facets of the new city through their eyes.
The next major chapter will drop on December 22, 2026. Further details and the specific timeframe will be announced as the launch date nears.

Chapter of the Year: Embers of the Everbright


One notable new addition to the update is the concept of the “Chapter of the Year.” Wuthering Waves normally plays its story out through episodic storylines centered around one version, but this time, it will present a “unified arc spanning a full year of in-depth storytelling.”
The development team has “strong confidence in its content volume, narrative quality, and long-term update cadence” for this upcoming season, and hopes that players will look forward to its story from its beginnings and throughout 2027.

item.title: Wuthering Waves’ 4.0 Announcement Teases What Looks to Be Another Lucia Expy
item.description:
Wuthering Waves Version 4.0 introduces Gordia, a character who bears a striking resemblance to Punishing: Gray Raven's Lucia. Read on to see our reaction to this character’s design and what it could mean for the game going forward.

Wuthering Waves’ 4.0 Announcement Teases What Looks to Be Another Lucia Expy


Lucia is Punishing: Gray Raven’s most recognizable character. Apologies to all the Alpha mains (myself included), Karenina fans, Vera worshippers, and Nanami enjoyers out there, but Lucia isn’t the game’s mascot for nothing.
That’s what makes Gordia, recently revealed through Wuthering Waves’ 4.0 Announcement (technically), so striking. At first glance, she looks like PGR’s most beloved character if she had a whip and a mean streak: the more visually blatant Lucia expy that many fans have been looking forward to for a long time.
Now, what exactly is an “expy”? While there’s no universally agreed-upon threshold for what constitutes one, the term itself is generally understood as shorthand for “exported character.” For the purposes of this article, we can generally categorize them into three kinds: Visual, Narrative, and Conceptual expys. Characters from HoYoverse-developed gacha games, in particular, provide plenty of examples of these categories, often with considerable overlap.
Yae Miko of Genshin Impact, for example, is primarily a visual expy of Yae Sakura from Honkai Impact 3rd, sharing recognizable design elements such as their long pink hair and fox motifs without necessarily sharing much of their character identities. An example of a conceptual expy, on the other hand, is Genshin Impact’s Raiden Shogun, who shares several conceptual and thematic elements with Raiden Mei, most notably their naming, lightning associations, and Kaminari-inspired imagery.
Wuthering Waves itself has had its fair share of expy comparisons, albeit with varying degrees of speculative backing. These range from the thematic and character-based similarities between Luna from PGR and Phrolova from WuWa, to the more visually oriented comparisons between Vera and Lupa/Yinlin. Not all of these comparisons are equally convincing, of course, but they demonstrate Kuro Games’ tendency and willingness to carry elements of its older character designs and concepts into its newer projects.

Recycling is Good if the Connections are Unique


Without knowing much about Gordia, all we can really assume is that she’s limited to being a visual expy of Punishing: Gray Raven’s Lucia. But why does that matter in the first place?
Well, we essentially already have a Lucia expy in Yangyang. She’s partly a visual one, but leans much more heavily to the narrative side as one of the protagonist’s earliest companions, having particularly strong protective streaks, being a constant source of belongingness, and so on.
Technically, however, you can imagine her as more of a homage-type character, as she shares traits with other members of the Gray Ravens like Lee and Liv.
Then, there’s also the “Mysterious Woman” who appears during the opening cutscene of the game, who also bears a striking resemblance to Lucia.
It matters because there will inevitably be identity-based conflict regarding these characters, especially if Kuro Games does follow up on its narrative promise of involving Yangyang more. While this may not be a concern for those who haven't touched Punishing: Gray Raven at all, players familiar with both games might find themselves comparing these characters against one another, particularly if they begin occupying similar narrative roles.
Of course, this isn't necessarily a bad thing. Characters can share inspirations without necessarily sharing identities. In fact, that's arguably the entire appeal of expys in the first place: taking recognizable elements from an existing character and reinterpreting them in a different setting. The important thing is ensuring that these characters have enough of their own identity to stand independently.
Yangyang, for instance, has her own history, motivations, and relationship with the Rover. Her similarities to Lucia don't invalidate those qualities, nor should they. The same should apply to Gordia. If anything, her introduction presents Kuro with another opportunity to demonstrate just how much mileage it can get out of an established and beloved character concept without simply reproducing the original. And if they can even provide a strong contrast from what players would expect from something designed similarly to their old character, then that's even better.
And maybe eventually, we’d get an actual Nanami expy that isn’t just a character (with lots of potential) swinging a chainsaw around—

item.title: GTA 6 Pre-Load Requires Up to 212GB of Storage, Rockstar Confirms
item.description:
Rockstar has outlined its pre-launch plans for GTA 6. Read on to learn when you can start downloading the game and prepare your console before its November 19 release.

GTA 6 Pre-Load Needs a Whopping 212GB of Free Space


PS5 and Xbox Pre-Load Times Confirmed for November 10


Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) will require up to 212 GB of available storage for pre-loading, according to Rockstar Games, which has confirmed that downloads will begin on November 10.
PlayStation 5 players can start pre-loading at midnight local time. Xbox Series X|S players, meanwhile, can begin globally on November 9 at 4:00 P.M. PT / 7:00 P.M. ET.
Players looking to purchase a physical edition can also expect code-in-box versions to arrive at retailers starting November 12. GTA 6 is scheduled to launch on November 19 for both consoles.
For more on the game's release date and time, check out our article below!

item.title: GTA 6 Might Just Sweep The Game Awards 2026, Fans Say
item.description:
GTA 6's launch trailer arrives, and its release date lands just inside The Game Awards 2026 eligibility window. Read on to learn more about the timeline, rules, and other details.

GTA 6 Gears Up for Release and Makes It to The Game Awards 2026 Cutoff


Launch Trailer Arrives as TGA 2026 Eligibility Rules Surface


Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6) revealed its official launch trailer on Rockstar Games’ X (Twitter), with a launch timeline that community members noted makes it eligible for The Game Awards 2026. The upbeat trailer introduces a new track, "Flower in a Hurricane," featuring prominent artists like Justice, Tame Impala, SZA, and King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard. Many welcomed the video with hype, with comments praising both the cinematic snippets and the new track.
According to The Game Awards' FAQ, a title must be commercially available by Friday, November 20, at 9 PM (PT) to qualify for the 2026 ceremony. GTA 6 beats that deadline by just one day, releasing on November 19, 2026 after a series of delays. GTA 6 is also eligible for the Players' Voice category, which accepts entries until November 30, 2026. The ceremony itself will take place on December 10, 2026, at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles.

Cutoff Follows Past Years, Not a Special Exception


Multiple viral posts claimed the show made room specifically for Rockstar's game, but an X Community Note highlighted that the November 20 cutoff mirrors previous years. It is verified that past deadlines include November 21 for 2025 and November 22 for 2024, placing GTA 6 fairly within the standard window to be qualified.
Additionally, eligibility is only the first step, as the FAQ notes that nominees in most categories are selected by an international jury of over 100 media and influencer outlets. The jury decides winners by a vote split between the jury (90%) and public fan voting (10%). To give later entries a chance, publishers can also provide review copies or pre-release access to help outlets meet the balloting deadlines.

Split Over Whether GTA 6 Will Sweep


Reactions to the news have been fairly mixed. Some fans predict GTA 6 will dominate the show, with a few joking that other 2026 releases won’t stand a chance. Others within the gaming community expressed frustration, arguing that the title could simply win on hype alone before players can put in enough hours to evaluate the gameplay fairly.
However, many still defend its placement in the lineup. One fan argues that GTA 6 is a legitimate 2026 release qualifying within the standard period and that losing to another 2026 title would take nothing away from a strong year for gaming. Fan votes also represent only a small portion of the final score, and the jury still holds the majority of the weight in deciding the wins.
Given the scale of GTA 6’s release, it goes without saying that other publishers have reconsidered changing up their games’ release dates. A few noteworthy titles, like Danganronpa 2x2 and Fable, are already suspected to have been affected, so it’s no surprise that Rockstar’s hit series has shaken up the gaming industry’s timeline. For more information on the game, check out the page below:

item.title: GTA 6 Extended Look Hypes Fans For Release With 26 Minutes of New Gameplay
item.description:
Grand Theft Auto VI has received a new gameplay showcase following its previously announced Netflix premiere. Learn more about the new gameplay mechanics, world details, and community reactions.

Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look


New Look at the Gameplay, Map Exploration, and Mechanics


Grand Theft Auto VI developer and publisher Rockstar Games has officially released an extensive gameplay showcase. Launching as a timed exclusive on Netflix, the 26-minute presentation captured entirely on PlayStation 5 gave fans their very first deep dive into actual gameplay mechanics, missions, and open-world activities across the state of Leonida.
The showcase opens with a high-stakes mission featuring dual protagonists Jason and Lucia, highlighting a dynamic cover system, cooperative character AI, and seamless switching mechanics reminiscent of Grand Theft Auto V. Throughout the video, players are treated to a massive assortment of open-world recreational activities—including scuba diving, jet skiing, kayaking, dirt biking, base jumping, street racing, club dancing, and visiting strip clubs.

Detailed Police Tracking, Mission Variety, and Relationship Mechanics


The gameplay footage confirmed several heavily requested features and systemic upgrades coming to the game. Alongside the return of the iconic six-star wanted level system, the game introduces a sophisticated police tracking mechanism featuring on-screen HUD identification icons. The police now actively track specific evidence such as your physical description, your vehicle, and your current clothing. To successfully shake the authorities, players must use tactical strategies like switching out getaway vehicles, changing clothes, or ditching hot cars so the police lose their specific tracking data.
Missions and open-world progression offer distinct new structural depths, with certain high-stakes assignments giving players multiple tactical approaches, flexible escape routes, or specific job splits where tasks can only be taken by one of the dual protagonists. Complementing these mission structures, Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson explained in an IGN interview that the game introduces a deeply integrated relationship system built around player choice. According to Nelson, players can choose how they want to handle Jason and Lucia's bond—whether that means nurturing their connection through shared moments like holding hands after leaving a store or opting out of the romantic side entirely without penalty. As Nelson noted, "Don’t bother with it if you aren’t. Up to you," clarifying that while the characters will always stay together as partners in crime for the narrative, extra relationship-building activities (like waiting for the other to get dressed, hanging out, or responding to texts) are entirely optional.
Additionally, players can interact with NPCs using a prompt system similar to Red Dead Redemption 2, pet or scold dogs to build karma, and manage various downtime activities like working out at gyms or watching satirical TV advertisements inside safehouses. The presentation also detailed complex melee combat, unique individual mission paths for Jason and Lucia, and intricate vehicle-entering mechanics.

Developer Insights on Immersion and Real-World Scale


Reflecting on the massive creative undertaking behind the project, The New York Times detailed how Rockstar approached the game's unprecedented fidelity and scale. Art director Aaron Garbut emphasized the studio's rigorous, hands-on approach to crafting the world, noting that instead of relying on procedural generation, developers art-directed non-player characters individually and packed rooms with bespoke details—from the tattoos on an NPC's arms to the specific drinks on a table.
Furthermore, developer Rob Nelson discussed the monumental technical challenge of bridging cinematic narrative and player freedom seamlessly. Comparing the studio's ambitions to a "moonshot," Nelson pointed out that allowing players to transition organically from daily safehouse routines like eating an apple or working out to high-stakes robberies and high-speed chases required completely reimagining how open-world systems interact. Rather than cutting away with black screens, the goal is to make every moment—whether on a mission or just exploring the swamps on an airboat—feel entirely continuous and transformative.

Netflix Streaming and Fans' Reactions


The Netflix showcase rollout successfully brought millions of viewers to the platform to catch the deep dive. The massive influx of eager fans tuning in all at once caused a temporary crash on Netflix, greeting users with error messages until access was restored.
The footage sparked an immediate wildfire of discussions across social media. Fans expressed overwhelming excitement over the gorgeous lighting, intricate physics, organic character banter, and relationship-shaping player choices like rushing Lucia's wardrobe changes, while internet forums heavily buzzed over details like the new evidence-based wanted icons, the return of the six-star system, and the depth of the game's open-world activities. With anticipation at an all-time high, Grand Theft Auto VI continues to cement its status as a once-in-a-generation cultural milestone ahead of its November release.

item.title: Arcane’s Sevika Was Pitched as a Wild Rift Champion, According to a Former Riot Developer
item.description:
Arcane's Sevika was pitched to debut as a Wild Rift champion but was overruled, according to a former Riot developer. Find out more details about the rejected pitch below.

Arcane’s Sevika Could Have Debuted as a Wild Rift Champion


A Former Riot Developer Says Her Sevika Pitch Was Overruled


Sevika from Arcane could have debuted as a Wild Rift champion, bringing Silco’s former lieutenant to the mobile version of League of Legends. Maddy Marquissee, the game’s former Champions Product Lead, said she "tried so hard" to make it happen and pitched Sevika for the roster but was ultimately overruled. Marquissee shared the detail on X (Twitter) on November 9 while responding to a fan who posted Sevika’s fight with the chem-baron Smeech from Arcane Season 2.
Fans in the thread were gutted that Sevika never made it onto the Wild Rift roster. Some felt she should have been given the same treatment as Ambessa and Mel Medarda, who both made the move from Arcane to both versions of LoL. One fan did ask Marquissee why the pitch had been overruled, and that question simply wasn't answered in the public thread.
Marquissee began working on Wild Rift while it was still in preproduction, helping develop tutorials and other features for new players. She later led the champions team and spoke publicly about Riot’s process for bringing Gwen over from PC League and reworking Karma for mobile, including a new ultimate. After leaving Riot, she now works at Wizards of the Coast as a principal product designer on Magic: The Gathering’s Secret Lair.
Norra, a portal-hopping yordle who arrived in February 2026, became the first champion to debut in Wild Rift and remains exclusive to its mobile roster. Players had already met her in Riot’s card game, Legends of Runeterra, and in Teamfight Tactics, where she shared a unit with her magical cat, Yuumi. In a follow-up thread, Marquissee called Norra "a great choice" and said the Wild Rift team killed it with their implementation.

Riot Has Already Experimented With a Playable Sevika


Sevika’s TFT Kit Ran on a Slot Machine


Fans have already seen how Sevika's lucky prosthetic arm would work in a game as TFT, where the kit was built around random attacks and random rewards. Sevika was one of the rarer recruits at launch in the League of Legends strategy spin-off, joining Into the Arcane as a 5 cost unit in November 2024.
Every time Sevika cast Beat the Odds her arm could produce a flamethrower, an extendable punch, or a chomp that would finish off a weakened enemy. A rare jackpot could yield gold or even a treasure chest. Her unique High Roller trait also gave her an extra roll for bonuses such as rockets, a shield, or more gold.
She and Smeech also shared the Chem-Baron trait where fielding enough Chem-Barons earned players Shimmer after fights, with bigger payouts during a losing streak. Players could then cash that Shimmer in for black-market gear. In a Riot post-set retrospective published on March 10, 2025, Riot Mort described Sevika and Smeech as "instant favorites." The article singled them out as two of the roster’s biggest successes, while other Arcane additions, including the enforcers Loris and Steb, struggled to generate the same enthusiasm.
Sevika is still one of the fan favorites in Arcane, and Riot could still very much bring her over to either version of League in the future. However, Arcane is over though and Riot are now looking at other stories across Runeterra. At the same time, 2XKO, a fighting game that seemed tailor-made for a brawler like Sevika, is winding down active development without her.
With the focus seems to be moving away from Piltover and Zaun, Marquissee's failed pitch at least gives us a taster of where the Wild Rift Sevika might have ended up.

item.title: Petit Planet Makes NPCs Come Alive With AI-Powered Conversations That Remember Players’ Coffee Orders
item.description:
Petit Planet uses generative AI so certain NPCs can remember players and draw from past conversations. Find out how HoYoverse will pair those interactions with human-written stories told through seasonal narratives.

Generative AI Powers Petit Planet’s Live NPC Conversations


AI NPCs Are One of Petit Planet’s Four Defining Features


Petit Planet has clarified how it will use generative AI in its upcoming cozy life simulation game after showcasing the feature throughout pre-release testing. Developer HoYoverse said its AI-powered NPCs will remember players and improvise conversations with characters such as Nalo, a barista in the game’s multiplayer hub, who can remember previous interactions and change how they respond when players return.
Lead game designer Murphy and lead artist Yinli Huang gave more details in a Famitsu interview published on November 9. Murphy named AI-powered NPCs as one of four features intended to distinguish Petit Planet from other life sims.
The other three features include long-term support shaped by the community, a planetary setting that encourages players to explore beyond their own worlds, and creation tools that cover everything from interiors and terrain to the color of the water and sky. HoYoverse also wants to give players a place to spend time with friends and meet new people.

Scenario Team Will Write Petit Planet’s Main Story


Huang explained that the developers assign every AI NPC a personality and set of values that guide the reactions and replies they generate, but reiterated that their own writers still handle the main story. "The game’s story is created from scratch by the scenario team," Huang said. "Generative AI is not used in that process."
An earlier beta report from Chinese outlet Chuapp showed that Nalo remembered a coffee order the writer had placed several days earlier while continuing to converse with other visitors. However, the character did not handle every exchange perfectly, as the report found that she could occasionally lose track of faster group conversations.
Huang also said HoYoverse plans to introduce more AI-powered NPCs, including a character named Amira Rabbit. She spoke at a November 6 media showcase ahead of G-STAR 2026, a major annual gaming convention in South Korea, according to a November 8 report from Inven Global.

Petit Planet Will Tell a New Story With Each Season


Seasons Will Last Longer Than Six Weeks


Petit Planet’s narrative will be told through seasonal stories, longer character arcs, and smaller events woven into everyday activities. Murphy explained that the Season of Snowfall shown during the media tour has its own storyline that takes players to a hot spring resort, and the next season will introduce another.
Additionally, the game’s neighbors will have personal stories that gradually unfold as players grow closer to them. Murphy said each neighbor has a long story and mentioned that a player might set out to fish and run into an unexpected narrative event along the way.
HoYoverse intends to give these stories more room than the six-week update cycles commonly used for its other games such as Genshin Impact, Honkai: Star Rail, and Zenless Zone Zero. Additionally, players who join partway through Season of Snowfall can still experience its complete story. While some neighbors may become temporarily unavailable once the season in which they first appear has ended, HoYoverse plans to create additional opportunities to meet them in later updates.
Petit Planet will launch for PC, iOS, and Android on December 4, with a Nintendo Switch 2 version scheduled for 2027. For players interested in HoYoverse's cozy game, check out our review below:

item.title: Nintendo To Discontinue Google And Apple Linking to Nintendo Accounts
item.description:
Nintendo announces discontinuation of Google and Apple account linking to Nintendo accounts, effective January 26, 2027. Read on to find out how to sign in and change details.

Nintendo Says Goodbye to Google and Apple Sign-In


Nintendo Accounts Are Now Exclusive To Email and Sign-In IDs


As announced by Nintendo on November 11, 2026, third-party sign in through Google and Apple for Nintendo accounts will be discontinued by January 26, 2027. By that date, new Nintendo accounts cannot be made through either service and must be made directly on the Nintendo website. The My Nintendo Platinum Points mission with Google linking will also be discontinued in line with the changes.
To sign in after its end of service, affected players must sign in using the dedicated email address, Sign-In ID, or a Passkey which requires the use of the player’s smart device with fingerprint of facial recognition in lieu of a password. All can be modified and changed in the official Nintendo account website.

item.title: Ocarina of Time Suggests a Majora’s Mask Remake Is Only a Matter of Time
item.description:
Ocarina of Time’s new remake includes several subtle nods to Majora’s Mask. Find out how these characters, mechanics, and Nintendo's history point toward a potential Majora's Mask remake.

The New Ocarina of Time Teases Majora’s Mask Connections


Returning Characters Look and Sound More Like Their Sequel Selves


The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake seems to lay the groundwork for a possible Majora’s Mask remake, although the company has yet to announce one. Released in 2000, Majora’s Mask is a direct sequel set several months after Ocarina of Time. It follows the same young Link and Epona into Termina, where the Happy Mask Salesman asks Link to recover the powerful mask Skull Kid stole.
The strongest evidence for a Switch 2 remake comes from the Happy Mask Salesman, a minor shopkeeper in Ocarina of Time who becomes a central figure in its sequel. His latest model wears gold cuffs absent from both earlier versions of Ocarina of Time, but present on him in the Nintendo 64 and 3DS versions of Majora’s Mask.
Additionally, his rewritten dialogue and considerably more unsettling presentation bring him closer to being the mysterious figure waiting inside the sequel’s Clock Town’s tower than the eccentric merchant of the first game.
Skull Kid is another recurring character who becomes the sequel’s central antagonist under the influence of Majora’s Mask. In the remake, players found that hitting him with the slingshot reportedly triggers the distinctive cackle he uses in Majora’s Mask, which was absent from any version of Ocarina of Time.

The Passage of Time is Central to the Sequel


Another reference appears when Link speaks to a Zora while wearing a mask. The Zora says, "Although I have heard tell of other cultures that make use of masks in their rituals." The remark echoes an early scene in Majora’s Mask, after Link returns to the Clock Tower without recovering the stolen mask. The Happy Mask Salesman then explains its history, describing Majora’s Mask as an accursed artifact once used by an ancient tribe in hexing rituals.
Encountering the Running Man while wearing the Bunny Hood reveals another connection. He describes it as the ears of a legendary rabbit "said to move like the wind," recalling its function in Majora’s Mask, where it increases Link’s running speed. Ocarina of Time doesn't grant Link the same benefit, but after the Running Man buys it, he sprints off much faster than before.
Also, a new feature of the Ocarina of Time remake is that the clock continues running inside towns and dungeons, with residents moving between their homes, workplaces, and evening routines as the day progresses. A more elaborate version of that idea sits at the heart of Majora’s Mask, which unfolds across a repeating three-day cycle in which every resident follows a set schedule.
However, speaking to Game Informer ahead of the remake’s release, Aonuma said staff members had asked about adding nods to Zelda’s timeline and references to other games. He recalled telling them, "No, let’s focus on this game. Let’s make this the best version of Ocarina of Time that we can." Although the timeline remained in the back of the team’s mind, Aonuma said the remake was not dealt with the intention of explicitly referencing other entries.
Still, the team managed to slip in subtle connections like Sheik's harp consistent with the one seen in Skyward Sword.

Nintendo Has Paired These Two Zelda Games Twice Already


Majora’s Mask Followed Ocarina of Time on N64 and 3DS


A new Majora’s Mask remake would follow a familiar pattern, as Nintendo has previously followed Ocarina of Time with its sequel. Majora’s Mask wasn't planned while Nintendo was developing Ocarina of Time.
Speaking with then-Nintendo president Satoru Iwata in a 2010 Iwata Asks interview about Super Mario Galaxy 2, Shigeru Miyamoto explained, "For Majora’s Mask, we simply adopted the 3D engine from Ocarina of Time." Nintendo reused that engine, along with many of the earlier game’s character models and underlying systems, before building a new world around its repeating three-day cycle.
Years later, Nintendo took a similar route with the 3DS remakes. Ocarina of Time 3D launched in June 2011, and work on Majora’s Mask 3D began "almost immediately" after development wrapped. Grezzo handled both remakes, although the second remained unannounced for more than three years. Nintendo finally revealed it in November 2014 and released it the following February.

Nintendo Rarely Lets a Good Foundation Go to Waste


Nintendo tends to build new games on existing foundations, carrying over engines, visual styles, and core systems rather than starting from scratch. Spirit Tracks retained Phantom Hourglass's touch-controlled framework, and Tears of the Kingdom retained Breath of the Wild’s version of Hyrule while redesigning Link’s abilities. Grezzo also returned for the Switch remake of Link’s Awakening, whose visual and gameplay approach later became the starting point for Zelda’s adventure in Echoes of Wisdom.
Additionally, after completing Super Mario Galaxy 2, Miyamoto proposed another because Nintendo had invested so much time in an engine that could serve as the foundation for a follow-up. Development began under the working title Mario Galaxy 1.5, with plans to reuse the original game’s spherical environments and finish the project within a year.
It eventually grew into a full sequel developed over two and a half years, with Miyamoto estimating that more than 90% of its courses were new. In Iwata Asks, Satoru Iwata connected the approach directly to Zelda, saying, "That’s been one of Miyamoto-san’s methods ever since we followed up Ocarina of Time with Majora’s Mask."
Ocarina of Time is widely regarded as one of the most influential games ever made, while Majora’s Mask never achieved the same mainstream reach. Its darker, more experimental approach has nevertheless earned it a devoted following among Zelda fans.
With Nintendo reporting a "very strong start" for the remake, the connections between the two games have once again left players looking beyond Hyrule toward Termina, and upward at the prospect of its unsettling moon rendered in the remake’s upgraded visuals. item.title: Wolfenstein 3 Confirmed, Will Be the Series’ First Mainline Game Since 2017
item.description:
Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at MachineGames, as confirmed by Xbox CEO Asha Sharma. Find out more details about the announcement and the studio behind it below.

Xbox Reveals Wolfenstein 3 With a Glimpse of Its Script and Its First Scene


Protagonist B.J. Blazkowicz and Fergus Return


Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at MachineGames, as Xbox CEO Asha Sharma confirmed in a November 12 post on X (Twitter) during Xbox's 25th anniversary celebrations. It will be the series’ first mainline game since 2017’s Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus.
Sharma shared a page from the first chapter, "Nazitraz," which shows protagonist B.J. Blazkowicz and his longtime comrade and friend, Fergus, in an interrogation room. The pair appears to be interrogating a man named Otto, a name that might ring a bell for fans of The New Colossus. If this is the same Otto Ackermann, the Nazi commander B.J. can kill in an optional New Orleans mission, Wolfenstein 3 may be treating his death as non-canon or playing with the timeline again.
Xbox, Bethesda, and MachineGames have yet to reveal gameplay, a release window, platforms, and any additional details regarding Wolfenstein 3.

MachineGames Returns to Wolfenstein With a Third Mainline Game


Image taken from MachineGames' X (Twitter) Post
MachineGames has also confirmed it is working on the game, with the studio sharing a motion-capture photo featuring Debra Wilson and Brian Bloom. In its November 13, 2026, post celebrating Xbox’s 25th anniversary, Bethesda confirmed that Wilson and Bloom will reprise their roles as Grace Walker and B.J. Blazkowicz, respectively.
The Swedish studio kicked off the series’ modern reboot with 2014’s Wolfenstein: The New Order, followed by the standalone prequel Wolfenstein: The Old Blood in 2015 and Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus in 2017. It also co-developed two 2019 spin-offs with Arkane Lyon, the co-op shooter Wolfenstein: Youngblood and the VR game Wolfenstein: Cyberpilot.
ZeniMax Media, Bethesda Softworks’ parent company, acquired MachineGames in 2010. Then, the studio became part of Xbox when Microsoft bought ZeniMax in 2021. More recently, MachineGames developed Indiana Jones and the Great Circle, which Bethesda Softworks published in December 2024.

Bethesda Celebrates Xbox 25 with id Software & MachineGames News

item.title: Nintendo Adds Game Gift-Giving Feature in eShop
item.description:
Nintendo will add a gift-giving system to the Nintendo eShop starting November 16th, 2026, allowing family group members to purchase digital games for one another.

Nintendo Introduces Digital Gift-Giving in eShop


From Family to Family Member


Nintendo adds a new gift-giving feature to the Nintendo eShop just in time for the holidays. The feature is set to go live on November 16th or 17th, 2026, depending on the eShop’s region, with the update for it now live on all devices ahead of its launch.
Eligible games, DLCs, and upgrade packs can be gifted by anyone to any family member in a family group they are a part of.
However, not all products may be gifted, and will depend on the developer or publisher’s individual discretion, and the number of digital gift purchases in a given time period (as of writing, still unannounced) is limited. Additionally, supervised accounts (restricted accounts usually given to children) are not allowed to send digital gifts.

Gifts Appear As Presents on the Home Screen


A fun feature of the gift-giving system is that after purchasing, it will appear immediately at the HOME page of the recipient’s device (or chosen device, if there is more than one) in the form of a wrapped gift box. The color of the gift box can be chosen between eight colors. Once received, it can be downloaded and played right away. Gifting a Nintendo eShop product can be done on the product page of any eligible game, DLC, or upgrade pack. After the feature is launched, a “Give as a Gift” checkbox will be available.
Nintendo closed off the announcement post with a “This feature is a great way to celebrate a special occasion with your kids. Happy gifting!” message, opening up a new avenue for gift giving during the holiday season.

Community Reactions Mixed, Hoping For Friends List Expansion


Response to the news has been mixed, with some people appreciating the upcoming feature, creating an avenue for families who may not have the luxury of being physically together during the season and are in long-distance relationships.
Majority of the community found it lacking, especially because it was only limited to the Nintendo family group, which has a maximum of eight people. Many have wished for it to extend to the player’s friend list, similar to other popular platforms like Steam which allow for gifting to not only friends but even strangers.
Others have said that it doesn’t completely beat the notion of physically opening gifts during the holidays, and since the post specifically mentioned gifts to kids, they thought that it would defeat the purpose of gift-giving.
Source:
Official Nintendo Site: Coming soon: Gift digital games to family group members

item.title: WoW Forever Casts Solo Leveling’s Aleks Le as Every Male Skyborne NPC
item.description:
WoW: Forever casts Solo Leveling star and prominent voice actor Aleks Le as two named characters and every male Skyborne NPC. Find out more about his announcement and his other roles across anime and games.

WoW: Forever Gave Aleks Le a Much Bigger Role Than He Expected


Le’s Voice Runs Through Two Named Characters and Every Male Skyborne NPC


World of Warcraft: Forever (WoW: Forever) has tapped Aleks Le, the English voice of Solo Leveling protagonist Sung Jinwoo, to voice Talaanis Shadowsong, Rorian the Dayseeker, and every male Skyborne NPC in the game. Le revealed his involvement in an X (Twitter) post on November 5, one day after Blizzard’s anticipated reimagining of WoW’s original Azeroth launched globally.
"I had no idea the extent of my role," Le wrote, expressing surprise that his work went beyond two named characters to include every male Skyborne NPC. This gives Le a recurring presence in Zephras Isle, the Skyborne starting zone created for the new playable race, and wherever they may be throughout Azeroth. "I’m honored to be part of this legendary title."

Aleks Le Has Become a Familiar Voice Across Newer Anime and Games


Le is a Los Angeles-based voice actor whose work spans anime and video games. He considers Zenitsu Agatsuma in Demon Slayer his first major role, describing it as his "first-ever gigantic role in terms of status and scope" in an interview with TheWrap. Since then, he has also lent his voice to Sung Jinwoo in Solo Leveling, including the action-RPG Solo Leveling: ARISE OVERDRIVE, Jiji in Dandadan, Thorfinn in Vinland Saga’s Netflix dub, and Manjiro "Mikey" Sano in Tokyo Revengers.
Gamers might recognize Le as Luke in Street Fighter 6, protagonist Makoto Yuki of Persona 3 Reload, Daredevil in Marvel Rivals, Mark Grayson in Invincible VS, and Sonon Kusakabe in Final Fantasy 7 Remake Intergrade.
Players who purchased the Skyborne Heroic Pack ($29.99) or a higher-tier edition will hear plenty of Aleks Le as they journey from Zephras Isle into the wider world of Azeroth. Check out our review for WoW: Forever below:

item.title: FF7 Remake Producer Still Wants a Screen Adaptation Nearly 30 Years After Directing the Original
item.description:
FF7 remake producer Yoshinori Kitase wants to see more Final Fantasy adaptations. Find out why he thinks that the remakes could inspire a new series based on the games.

Final Fantasy Producer Is Open to More TV Adaptations


Kitase Points to FF7’s Expanded World


Yoshinori Kitase, producer of the Final Fantasy VII remake (FF7) trilogy, would like to see more Final Fantasy stories on television. He sees the world Square Enix expanded in the remakes as a starting point for future adaptations.
When IGN asked at Lucca Comics & Games 2026 whether Square Enix was still interested in film and other adaptations, Kitase said the remakes explored far more of FF7's world than the original game. He said he’d welcome "games or TV series inspired by the story of Final Fantasy."
In the past, he raised the idea of a FF7 film or TV show in January 2025, telling Danny Peña on Gamertag Radio that he’d heard about Hollywood directors and actors who played the game, calling the prospect of seeing one of those creators make an adaptation "strictly my personal sort of wish."

The Cycle of Influence From Star Wars to Expedition 33


In IGN’s interview, Kitase pointed out how Final Fantasy developed its own style by bringing influences from Japanese manga and anime into its early European-inspired settings. He’d spoken with the creators of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, Sandfall Interactive, and was happy to see how they’d drawn on Final Fantasy to make a game of their own.
The producer described it as a "cycle where we inspire each other," recalling how George Lucas’s Star Wars films influenced his own work. He even named Biggs and Wedge in Final Fantasy VI after two Rebel pilots. Additionally, the podrace in The Phantom Menace also gave him the idea of putting a sport inside a fantasy world, which led to Blitzball in Final Fantasy X.
Kitase said he and other developers who worked on the 1997 original still felt strongly about FF7. The remakes gave them a chance to build something new around it and let new players discover what longtime fans loved. For him, much of the series’ appeal comes from watching its characters change over the course of a game. When asked to pick a favorite among the games he’d worked on, he said 7 might be "the one I feel more attached to."

Final Fantasy’s Films Found Their Footing With Advent Children


Advent Children’s Ties to the Remake Trilogy


Final Fantasy has told stories outside the games for decades, starting with the 1994 anime Legend of the Crystals, which returned to the world of Final Fantasy V two centuries after the game. Its first theatrical film, 2001’s Final Fantasy: The Spirits Within, was such a box-office flop that it made Enix think twice about a merger it was already considering with Square, according to former Enix chairman Yasuhiro Fukushima in a 2003 interview with Mainichi Interactive, as reported by RPGamer.
Despite that, the companies went ahead with the merger in 2003. Two years later, Square Enix returned to film with Advent Children, a sequel to FF7 in which a mysterious illness and the return of old enemies draw Cloud Strife out of seclusion. It became a home video hit, with Sony Pictures Home Entertainment reporting 4.1 million copies shipped by 2009, when the expanded Advent Children Complete arrived on Blu-ray.
It’s still Final Fantasy’s most successful film project, and nearly two decades after its original release, Square Enix brought the expanded cut to U.S. theaters the week before FF7 Rebirth launched in 2024. It even influenced the upcoming finale, as Revelation director Naoki Hamaguchi told Anime News Network at Tokyo Game Show 2026 that the team had "definitely added connections to Advent Children," alongside ties to Crisis Core and other FF7 titles.
As the remake trilogy draws to a close in 2027, Kitase sees room for more Final Fantasy adaptations. After more than a decade spent expanding the world of FF7, it's up to him whether he still has a story to tell in Midgar or explore one of the series' other worlds. item.title: NIKKE Offers 20 Free Pulls and an Apology Following PC Launcher Malware Attack
item.description:
NIKKE officially apologized with in-game compensation and added a scanner after its PC launcher was used to spread malware since October 30. Find out what publisher Level Infinite says happened and what players can do.

Level Infinite Apologizes and Releases Its Timeline of the NIKKE Launcher Attack


PC Players May Have Been Compromised Since October 30


Goddess of Victory: NIKKE has issued a public apology on its official X (Twitter) account after confirming that attackers tampered with files used in the game’s PC launcher. In the November 5 statement, publisher Level Infinite took responsibility for the security failure and acknowledged that the incident put players’ computers and personal information at risk. "An official program intended to let players enjoy the game should never become a threat to their safety," the NIKKE Operations Team wrote.
Developer Shift Up CEO Kim Hyung-tae issued a separate apology on November 4, saying the developer was working with Level Infinite and "dedicating all our resources to identifying a fundamental solution." Meanwhile, players received in-game compensation; X users under the post shared a screenshot of the in-game compensation notice, listing 3,000 Gems, 10 Advanced Recruit Vouchers, and a bundle of upgrade materials. These materials and gems should cover 10 pulls, and the vouchers for another 10, for a total of 20. Players can use either on limited-time banners like the ones NIKKE ran during its Persona crossover.
Image taken from NIKKE's official website
According to Level Infinite, an as-yet-unknown third party took control of a domain used by some of its game services on September 27. Later that day, four scripts the launcher downloaded from the publisher’s servers were altered. According to their timeline, those scripts began delivering malware to players’ PCs on October 30 at 3:52 a.m. (UTC+9), a day after the fourth anniversary update launched. The team says it detected the tampering around midnight on November 4, replaced three of the scripts within a few hours, and refreshed the server cache for the fourth time later that day.
However, independent researcher MotherSphere cited a player’s launcher log indicating that the remote-access malware had already run on October 23 UTC, or October 24 at 1:40 a.m. in the time zone Level Infinite uses. In this timeline posted on November 4, the reported case started more than six days before the publisher’s stated start date.

Official PC Launcher Adds a Malware Scanner


Level Infinite Will Review Reports of Financial Loss


Level Infinite says the current version of NIKKE’s PC launcher is safe to use after the company fixed the affected files and ran additional checks. It is asking anyone who opened the Windows launcher at least once since September 27 at 3:41 p.m. (UTC+9) to check their PC and accounts. Fortunately, the publisher confirms the native Android and iOS versions were unaffected.
On their end, the November 5 update added a scanner that checks for malware tied to the incident when players start the Windows client. If the scan detects the malware, the client asks for permission to remove the associated files and registry entries. Players who have already uninstalled the launcher, or who prefer to check without reopening it, can follow NIKKE’s manual guide on their website.
Alongside the in-game rewards announced for all players, Level Infinite is asking anyone who suspects an account with another service was compromised or who suffered a financial loss to contact customer support. "We will review each inquiry carefully and respond as promptly as possible," the publisher wrote, as its investigation into the extent of the damage is ongoing.
Despite Level Infinite’s assurances, players are understandably frustrated that opening the official PC launcher left them checking their PCs for malware and wondering what happened to their personal information. For more on the game itself, check out our Goddess of Victory: NIKKE review below.

item.title: God of War Laufey Delayed to May 20, 2027 to Reach Its "Fullest Potential"
item.description:
God of War Laufey has been delayed to 2027. Learn more about the delay and the upcoming God of War game's release date.

God of War Laufey Release Moved to May 2027


Faye's Journey Through Everywhen Needs More Development Time


God of War Laufey will now launch on May 20, 2027, three months later than its previously announced February 16 release date. Santa Monica Studio confirmed the delay on November 4 and said the team needs more time to complete development and push it to "its fullest potential." The studio thanked fans for their patience and promised to share more updates soon.
Since it was first revealed during the PlayStation State of Play June 2026, GoW Laufey was met with a lot of criticism, mostly due to it being a God of War title not being headlined by Kratos. Recently, fans also came down on the GoW Laufey Collector Box being priced at $149.99 and not including the actual game.

Dodging a Loaded February 2027 Lineup


While some were disappointed with the delay, other fans were glad that GoW Laufey's release date will be moved further. Players noted that February 2027 is already jam-packed with big titles, and the upcoming GoW spin-off deserved its own spotlight.
Several JRPGs, such as Romancing SaGa 3: Destinies United and Atelier Karia: The Night Kingdom & the Guide of Memories, will be launching that month, along with highly anticipated remakes like Persona 4 Revival and Yu-Gi-Oh! Tag Force GX. Additionally, major franchise titles like Metro 2039 and Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis are also releasing in February, and the month will be capped off by what is probably the biggest game of the month: the open-world action-RPG reboot of Fable.
Santa Monica Studio has been quite busy with the God of War franchise, with its most recent launch being God of War: Sons of Sparta in February 2026. They are also currently in production on a God of War trilogy remake, which will see the return of Kratos' original voice actor, TC Carson. To find out more details about God of War: Laufey, check out our article below.
Sources:
Santa Monica Studio X post on God of War Laufey Release Date Delay
PlayStation Blog: Collector Box contents, price, release date and availability
